source.title: Some open problems on best approximation in normed linear spaces

accepted.question_text: Let E be an m-dimensional Banach space with 3 <= m < infinity. Must there exist a one-dimensional linear subspace G of E such that every x in E has a unique best approximation in G; equivalently, must every such E contain a one-dimensional Chebyshev subspace?
accepted.context_brief: One-dimensional Chebyshev subspaces in finite-dimensional Banach spaces

evidence.quote: Does every m-dimensional Banach space E, where 3 <= m < oo , possess a one-dimensional Cebysev subspace G (dim E = n , dim G = 1) ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a separable Banach space that has no Chebyshev subspace at all, meaning no linear subspace G for which every point of the ambient space has a unique best approximation in G?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of separable Banach spaces with no Chebyshev subspace

evidence.quote: Does there exist a separable Banach space which has no Cebysev subspace ?

accepted.question_text: In the Banach space C([0,1]) of continuous scalar-valued functions on the interval [0,1], does there exist a Chebyshev subspace G whose dimension is infinite and whose codimension dim(C([0,1])/G) is also infinite?
accepted.context_brief: Infinite-dimensional and infinite-codimensional Chebyshev subspaces of C([0,1])

evidence.quote: Does the space C([0 , 1]) possess a Cebysev subspace of infinite dimension and infinite codimension (codim G = dim E/G) ?

accepted.question_text: Characterize, in purely topological terms, the compact spaces Q for which the complex Banach space C(Q) of continuous complex-valued functions on Q with the supremum norm contains a finite-dimensional Chebyshev subspace of dimension n > 1. Equivalently, characterize the compact spaces Q that admit a complex Chebyshev system x1, ..., xn with n > 1, meaning that every nontrivial linear combination of these functions has at most n - 1 zeros on Q.
accepted.context_brief: Topological characterization for finite-dimensional Chebyshev subspaces of complex C(Q)

evidence.quote: Characterize (topologically) those compact spaces Q for which the complex space C(Q) (of all continuous functions on Q with ||x|| = max |x(q)| ) contains a Cebysev subspace of finite dimension n > 1 .
Thus the above problem amounts to the following : Characterize (topologically) those compact spaces Q which admit a Cebysev system x1 , ... , xn with n > 1 .

accepted.question_text: Characterize, in purely topological terms, the compact spaces Q for which the real Banach space C_R(Q), or alternatively the complex Banach space C(Q), contains a Chebyshev subspace of finite codimension n >= 1.
accepted.context_brief: Topological characterization for finite-codimensional Chebyshev subspaces of C(Q)

evidence.quote: Characterize (topologically) those compact spaces Q for which the real space C_R(Q) [or the complex space C(Q) ] contains a Cebysev subspace of finite codimension n >= 1 .

accepted.question_text: Characterize those Banach spaces E for which there is no closed linear subspace G of finite codimension n < infinity such that some point x in E \ G has no best approximation in G, that is, P_G(x) = emptyset. Equivalently, characterize the Banach spaces E for which no such finite-codimensional subspace G admits a nonzero vector z outside G satisfying ||z - g|| >= ||z|| for every g in G.

evidence.quote: Characterize those Banach spaces E which contain no closed linear subspace G with codim G = n < oo , with the following property : The set of all best approximation of x, P_G(x) = \phi (x in E \ G) ;
or, equivalently : such that there does not exist z in E \ {0} with z notin G , ||z - g|| >= ||z|| (g in G) .

accepted.question_text: Characterize those Banach spaces in which every Chebyshev set is convex.

evidence.quote: the following problem arises naturally : Characterize those Banach spaces in which every Cebysev set is convex.

accepted.question_text: For each finite dimension n > 3, characterize the n-dimensional Banach spaces E for which every Chebyshev set in E is convex.
accepted.context_brief: Finite-dimensional n > 3 case of convexity of Chebyshev sets

evidence.quote: BRONDSTED [3] has also solved the above characterization problem for n = 3 ... For n > 3 , the problem is still open.

accepted.question_text: In a Hilbert space H, must every Chebyshev set be convex?
accepted.context_brief: Convexity of Chebyshev sets in Hilbert spaces

evidence.quote: even the answer to the following question is unknown : In a Hilbert space H , is every Cebysev set necessarily convex ?

accepted.question_text: In a smooth uniformly convex Banach space, is every Chebyshev set weakly closed?
accepted.context_brief: Weak closedness of Chebyshev sets in smooth uniformly convex spaces

evidence.quote: the problem of convexity of Cebysev sets in smooth uniformely convex Banach spaces is equivalent to each of the following problems : (a) Is a Cebysev set weakly closed ?

accepted.question_text: In a smooth uniformly convex Banach space, is every Chebyshev set approximatively compact?
accepted.context_brief: Approximative compactness of Chebyshev sets in smooth uniformly convex spaces

evidence.quote: the problem of convexity of Cebysev sets in smooth uniformely convex Banach spaces is equivalent to each of the following problems : (b) Is a Cebysev set approximatively compact ?

accepted.question_text: If G is a Chebyshev set and the metric projection pi_G that sends each point x to its unique best approximation in G is weakly continuous, must pi_G also be strongly continuous?
accepted.context_brief: Weak versus strong continuity of the metric projection onto a Chebyshev set

evidence.quote: it is not known whether the weak continuity of pi_G , where G is a Cebysev set, implies its strong continuity.

accepted.question_text: Let H be a Hilbert space and let A be a closed convex subset of H with the property that every y in H has a unique farthest point in A, meaning a point of A at maximal distance from y. Must A consist of exactly one point?
accepted.context_brief: Unique farthest-point property in Hilbert spaces

evidence.quote: If a closed convex set A c H has the property that every y in H admits a unique farthest point in A (i. e. which has maximal distance from y ), does A necessarily consist of one simple point ?

needs_review.question_text_raw: How to combine the spaces c_0 and L^1([0,1]) in order to obtain a separable Banach space which has no Chebyshev subspace?

evidence.quote: Thus it is natural to ask the following problem : How to combine the spaces c_0 and L^1([0 , 1]) in order to obtain a separable Banach space which has no Cebysev subspace ?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Similar problem for complex L^1(T, nu) spaces.

evidence.quote: Other problems. 1° Similar problem for complex L^1(T , nu) spaces.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Extension to dim P_G(x) <= k (x in E \ G).

evidence.quote: 2° Extension to dim P_G(x) <= k (x in E \ G) .

Moved to needs_review because the instruction to 'combine' c_0 and L^1([0,1]) is too informal to rewrite into a mathematically precise standalone problem without adding unsupported detail.
Moved to needs_review because 'Similar problem for complex L^1(T, nu) spaces' points back to preceding context instead of stating the actual problem explicitly.
Moved to needs_review because the terse extension statement does not explicitly identify the base problem or the full ambient setting needed for a self-contained rewrite.
